title: Prediction Fairness Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning Analytics Ethics
Bias in Prediction
Mastery Prediction
Small-Group Suppression
Data Visualization
description: A Chart.js grouped bar chart of a mastery prediction's under- and over-estimation rates for three synthetic learner groups (pointer users, keyboard users, shared device), with dashed pooled-average lines, three scenarios (even error, hidden gap, small group) and a suppression threshold that hides small groups. All numbers are synthetic.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Comparing prediction error across learner groups
learningObjectives: The learner will critique a mastery prediction by comparing its error across learner groups, and decide whether a pooled average hides a gap.
prerequisites: Mastery prediction and held-out assessment (Chapters 18 and 19)
Bias in prediction and the suppression threshold (Chapters 21 and 24)

accessibility.notes: Native labeled controls; the chart canvas has role=img and an aria-label summarizing current values; a screen-reader-only data table is updated with every change; the message area is an aria-live region; blue and orange series are a color-blind-safe pair and the pooled lines differ in dash pattern

controls.label: Scenario
controls.purpose: Choose Even error, Hidden gap or Small group

controls.label: Threshold
controls.purpose: Hide any group with fewer learners than the threshold

controls.label: Show pooled average
controls.purpose: Show or hide the pooled under- and over-estimation lines

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return to Hidden gap, threshold 10, pooled lines on

simulation.model: Per-group error rates computed from synthetic counts; pooled rate = total errors / total learners
equations: group rate = errors in group / learners in group
pooled rate = sum of errors / sum of learners
assumptions: All counts are invented to illustrate the method; no real learner data exists
A gap of 10 or more percentage points above the pooled rate is flagged

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Critique of a summary statistic by disaggregation
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Scenario comparison with a threshold slider and feedback messages
keyQuestions: Does the pooled error rate describe every group fairly?
In which direction is each group mis-estimated?
What does suppressing a small group protect, and what does it hide?
commonMisconceptions: An acceptable pooled error means the model is fair to every group
Suppression has no cost for fairness analysis
Under- and over-estimation can be merged into one error number without loss
assessmentOpportunities: Stating whether each scenario hides a gap, with group, direction and size
